approaches.name: Geospatial least-cost electrification planning with remote mini-grid monitoring
approaches.description: The project uses geospatial least-cost rollout planning to site mini-grids in conflict-affected areas and a digital platform to remotely monitor their performance. Practices: Geospatial least-cost electrification rollout plan used to select sites in conflict-affected territories; Digital platform for remote mini-grid performance monitoring.
approaches.why_innovative: Digital core: geospatial rollout plan | New: spatial targeting of neglected conflict territories | Adoption: incorporated in finalized plan and site selection | category Technological; adoption apply; judged in 1 round(s); final check: digital core, in_use before 2019

evidence.text: This has been incorporated in the recently finalized geospatial electrification rollout plan and in the selection of sites to be electrified.

extra_evidence.text: One of the solutions identified is an adjustment to the spatial distribution of investments, through additional investment in neglected or marginalized territories, with potentially multisector projects supporting the deployment of infrastructure, services, and governance systems across territories, focusing on territorial and social inclusion.
Communities in both conflict and high conflict risk territories will be provided with access to electricity under the project.

It would support AMADER’s Technical assistance in project management and supervision of works, communication, and the development of the digital platform for the collection and analysis of data to ensure remote performance monitoring of individual mini-grids.

category.rationale: Technological: geospatial analysis is the core targeting mechanism

sector.rationale: Geospatial least-cost electrification planning targets solar-based access rollout, aligning with the dominant solar sector.

replication.evidence: Africa Regional Energy Trade DPF Program (P171225), MESIP (P166796), REHSP (131084), and the FCS RE Segou Solaire Mali Project (P148355). The World Bank has also been supporting several investment projects aimed at expanding access to electricity in the region: Guinea- Mali Interconnection Project (P166042) and Regional Off-Grid Electricity Access Project (ROGEAP, P160708) or ECOWAS-Regional Elect
